scenario.title: Operation Torch
intro.text:
OPERATION TORCH - 24 AUG 1949

East of Mt Grammos, Pindus Mountains

We are on the verge of winning the war! The defeated rebels have been entrenched in the mountains at the Albania border and the General Staff has ordered a last major operation in order to complete our victory. The Americans have supplied us with modern dive bomber and they should help to destroy the strong fortifications. Chase off the remaining communist troops from their fortifications in the Grammos mountains!

GOAL Capture all VH!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-19-0-briliant.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.reaction-19-0-briliant.text: The Vitsi objectives fell before the DSE could transfer its main body. The government now speaks of a final campaign as if one successful sector had already designed it.
line.reaction-19-1-victory-tactical.text: The zone was broken, but detachments escaped toward the higher massifs. We hold the towns; the final operation will be fought against what left them.
line.callback-0.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.callback-0.text: The communiqué named the Vitsi towns before the dust settled. DSE detachments kept moving beyond them without waiting to be named. We have both reports this time.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: Closing the Vitsi routes trapped more detachments and brought more night searches. The villages remember which achievement arrived at their doors.
line.callback-2.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.callback-2.text: The Konitsa scouts remained a formation and entered Vitsi already knowing which tracks a conventional map ignores.
line.callback-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-3.text: The Konitsa patrols disappeared into the line units. Their knowledge spread, though no separate troop remained to challenge a bad headquarters map.
line.athens-control-debt.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.athens-control-debt.text: Hale wrote last month. British matériel has become American matériel, and every crate still arrives with a policy attached. He called that continuity. I think he meant it as an apology.
line.athens-corridor-debt.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.athens-corridor-debt.text: Markou sent the names of three families who crossed our Athens corridors. She also sent the names of two men later taken from their homes. She did not add a conclusion for us.
line.scene-0.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.scene-0.text: We possess the superiority we lacked in every earlier year: men, aircraft, guns, and an open supply line. I intend to use it once and finish this.
line.scene-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-1.text: Prisoner leaflets are already blowing back across our positions. They promise fair treatment. The local police have added names in pencil beside the promise.
line.scene-2.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.scene-2.text: Then remove the pencils and discipline the police. Do not confuse misconduct with an argument for leaving the DSE an army.
line.scene-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-3.text: The operational question remains. Seal every exit and destroy the formations, or leave controlled corridors for surrender and assign troops to protect them from both sides.
line.decision.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.decision.text: Commander, this is the last plan we write together. Which order can your formations carry without becoming something else?
line.decision.choice.close-the-ring.text: Close the ring and commit every gun to destroying organised resistance.
line.decision.choice.close-the-ring.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.
line.decision.choice.offer-surrender-cor: Publish surrender guarantees and keep controlled corridors open.
Spend 150 prestige and restore the core to full strength with full fuel and ammunition.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-0.text: Close the ring, then. Some men across it will hear artillery and decide the border is kinder than surrender. We should at least know why they ran.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-a-1.text: Air and artillery deny movement; ground forces close by phase. No secondary missions, no local bargains, no gaps left for another season of war.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-b-0.text: Corridors consume combat strength and offer the enemy another route to deceive us. I accept them because you will command them, not because I trust the slogans on the leaflets.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: Terms go by radio and leaflet. Units on the corridors answer to military law; prisoners are registered before local authorities touch them. Manesis, choose the sergeants.
line.choice-b-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-2.text: I already have. They are the ones least eager for the job.
epilogue.government-control-ring-success: The operations room is empty except for the surrender map and two locked cabinets of names. Papagos has announced the end of organised resistance. We did not fight Britain in Athens, and the larger war we feared never came. That does not open the prisons or bring the exiles home. I can defend why we obeyed. I can no longer pretend obedience settled the account.
epilogue.government-corridors-ring-succe: I found three families from the Athens corridors in a village below Grammos. They remembered your maps. One of their sons was in the prison column we passed an hour later. The army survived, Britain was never made our enemy, and the civil war is ending. If the government calls everything that follows security, those saved families will know exactly what the word conceals.
epilogue.government-control-surrender-su: The last corridor delivered fighters without rifles, wounded men on doors, and two officers still arguing over rank. That is a better return than a ravine full of bodies. In Athens we accepted British command because the alternative looked like military ruin and perhaps a war far beyond Greece. We escaped that danger. The guards closing the camp gate remind us that escaping one danger does not make every later order honourable.
epilogue.government-corridors-surrender-: The sergeants from the surrender posts have brought me their registers. No blanks, no men handed over without a name. We kept corridors in Athens and opened them again here. That saved lives. It did not decide what the police will do with those lives tomorrow. You kept faith with the soldiers under your order, Commander. The country will now test whether that was enough.
There is a red pencil gap on every copy of the encirclement map. Formations escaped through it, and the casualty telephone has not stopped. We once accepted British command because we feared defeat, isolation, and a wider war no Greek cabinet could control. We did avoid that war. We did not avoid this one, and obedience has offered no refuge from the result.
epilogue.government-corridors-ring-defea: The ring opened under attack and the villages are filling with search parties. I still meet people who lived because your Athens corridors stayed on the gun maps. They ask whether the same army has forgotten how to distinguish a road from a trap. I have no answer for them. The war continues, and restraint remembered is not restraint practised.
epilogue.government-control-surrender-de: The surrender loudspeakers are still on the trucks. Few heard them before the attack failed. We preserved this army under British command and told ourselves preservation would keep later choices in Greek hands. Today Greek headquarters chose, Greek battalions paid, and the decision still escaped us. The lesser danger was real. So is everything it failed to prevent.
epilogue.government-corridors-surrender-: We brought back wounded from both sides through the corridor and lost the ground beyond it. Headquarters calls that a failure, which is fair. The men ask whether the war would be over if we had been less careful. I told them I did not know. It is the first honest answer I have given them in some time.
